observations: Photo 0 shows a disassembled automotive engine component, dark plastic/metal housing with attached hoses and a multi-pin wiring connector (appears to be an air intake duct or sensor housing).
A visible watermark reads 'FAMOUS AUTO PARTS' across the image, seller's own branding, not a product brand.
No manufacturer name, part number, or vehicle make/model is legible anywhere on the part.
Connector pins are visible but no continuity, resistance or power test is shown.
Surface shows oxidation/discoloration on metal bracket and connector housing, consistent with a used/salvaged part.
No overall engine bay or vehicle context shown to confirm fitment vehicle.

identity.kind: used engine air intake housing with wiring harness connector (auto part)

claims.claim: "We offer all our clients 5 star☆ service (never buy an item because it's cheap...)"
claims.evidence: No photo supports or contradicts a service-quality claim; it is marketing language, not a verifiable product fact.

risks.risk: Electrical/sensor functionality of the connector and housing is unproven.
risks.proof: A clip showing the part powered/tested with a multimeter or on a running engine.

risks.risk: Exact vehicle make/model/year compatibility is unknown, which affects value.
risks.proof: A photo of any stamped part number or a photo showing the part still mounted in an identifiable engine bay.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unverified-fitment used part

risks.risk: Hidden cracks, broken mounting tabs, or missing clips not visible from this single angle.
risks.proof: Additional photos from multiple angles including the underside and all mounting points.

risks.risk: Corrosion on connector pins could indicate water damage affecting the attached sensor.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the connector pins and sensor tip.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of any stamped part number or label on the housing.
Photo of the connector pins in close focus.
Multiple angle photos (top, bottom, side) showing all mounting points.
A short clip of continuity/power test on the electrical connector if sold as functional.
response.reason: The item is clearly a used automotive engine component (air intake/sensor housing) that can be priced at worst case as an untested, fitment-unconfirmed used part; no model number is needed since it is identified by type, and the seller's service claim is marketing, not a product condition claim.
